steps.path: The version chip, the update popup, Settings → Help & feedback and the close-window prompt
steps.headline: This is what done means for automatic updates.

rows.statement: Install updates automatically can be switched off in Settings or the update popup, beside Get beta builds, and both stay in sync.
The switch looks like Get beta builds, with a circular-arrows icon and the description "Downloads new versions by itself", and starts on.
Get beta builds and Install updates automatically sit together under their own Updates heading in Help & feedback.
Once an update has downloaded, the version chip keeps its yellow pulse.
Once an update has downloaded, the version chip still shows the version and says it is ready and a restart is needed.

rows.statement: The update popup says Update ready, that it installs when you next quit, and offers Restart to update from one version to the next.
Where installing needs a password, the popup says restarting asks for it, and quitting never pops up a password box.
On package installs, a password box appears only after you press Restart to update, never without you asking.
With the switch off, the popup line reads "Downloaded. Restart when you are ready." and changes the moment you flip the switch.
Pressing Restart to update while chats are open shows the standard close prompt with the Resume on Next Launch switch.
rows.note: just show the standard closeout prompt that offers to resume sessions and stuff. if a user chooses not to exit by closing the prompt, cancel the restart.

rows.statement: Closing that prompt with the X cancels the restart and leaves the app running.

rows.statement: The restart prompt is titled Restart to update, says restarting ends your active sessions, and its red button reads Restart.
A broken release is pulled by removing its signed list; apps stop offering it and drop it before installing if already downloaded.
People on a pulled release see no automatic message; any notice goes out through the announcement chip when worthwhile.
